issues.legal_issue: Compensation determined and received for the compulsory acquisition of depreciable business assets is taxable as a balancing charge in the year of receipt even though a claim for enhanced compensation remains pending.
material_facts: The business assets were compulsorily acquired and possession was transferred to the acquiring authority.
The authority determined and paid compensation for the acquired assets, and the recipient accepted the payment while reserving its right to seek more.
A dispute over the market value and a claim for additional compensation remained pending before an adjudicating authority.
The tax authority treated the compensation received as proceeds from the acquired depreciable assets and calculated a balancing charge.
issues.conclusion: The compensation determined and received was taxable as business income in the year of receipt notwithstanding the pending claim for additional compensation. The addition was justified, and the question was answered in favour of the revenue.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 41(2) of the Income-tax Act, 1961, read with Section 32(1A) and the explanation to Section 32(1)(iii), compensation for compulsory acquisition is included within the relevant money payable and the acquisition is treated as a sale for calculating the balancing charge. Once compensation is determined and paid, it is compensation payable for the acquired assets; a pending dispute seeking additional compensation does not postpone taxation of the amount already received. Any additional compensation received later is taxable in the year it is received. The Court relied on the accrual principle discussed in CIT v. The Central Indian Electric Supply Co. Ltd. and Kesoram Industries & Cotton Mills Ltd.; it distinguished the capital-receipt discussion in CIT v. Bipinchandra Maganlal & Co. Ltd. because the governing statutory fiction treats the amount as business income for tax purposes. Sections 41(1) and 41(4) also support taxing recoveries in the year they are received.

rule.if: balancing_charge_assessment and compulsorily_acquired_depreciable_business_assets and compensation_determined_and_received and enhancement_claim_pending

predicates.balancing_charge_assessment: The proceeding concerns whether a balancing charge on proceeds from business assets is taxable.
predicates.compulsorily_acquired_depreciable_busine: An authority compulsorily acquired depreciable assets used in the taxpayer's business.
predicates.compensation_determined_and_received: The acquiring authority determined compensation for the assets and the taxpayer received it.
predicates.enhancement_claim_pending: The taxpayer continued to dispute the valuation and seek additional compensation.

issues.definition: When a balancing-charge assessment concerns compulsorily acquired depreciable business assets, compensation has been determined and received, and a claim for enhancement remains pending, the received compensation is taxable in the year of receipt.
